jobs.description:
Your job

As a Saltmarsh Ecology Researcher, you will contribute to the saltmarsh research programme at Wageningen Marine Research (WMR). Working closely with the saltmarsh team, you will carry out field measurements and analyses to investigate long-term vegetation dynamics and sediment accretion, the impacts of land subsidence caused by gas extraction, and carbon sequestration in saltmarsh ecosystems. You will translate this knowledge into reports and provide advice on saltmarsh restoration plans and management strategies. In doing so, you will also contribute to the development of nature-based solutions for coastal areas and to understanding how these can be implemented in an ecologically responsible manner.

You will work with colleagues on several projects simultaneously, with responsibilities allocated according to capacity and individual interests. Engagement with clients and other stakeholders is an integral part of our work.

Your Responsibilities As a Saltmarsh Ecology Researcher Include

carrying out annual monitoring of sediment accretion and vegetation development across various saltmarshes in the Wadden Sea;
analysing and interpreting monitoring data;
writing reports for clients;
assisting in the acquisition of new projects and the preparation of research proposals;
publishing and presenting your research in scientific journals and at conferences.

Wageningen Marine Research

Your primary area of work will be the Dutch Wadden Sea, although opportunities may also arise to contribute to projects elsewhere in the Netherlands and internationally. Wageningen Marine Research (https://www.wur.nl/en/about-wur/our-research/wageningen-marine-research) (WMR) is a leading organisation in the Netherlands in the field of marine ecological data collection, covering benthic fauna, marine mammals, fish, birds, coral, shellfish, and more. Many of these datasets have been collected and maintained using standardised methodologies for decades. In this role, you will contribute to the continuation and development of the saltmarsh monitoring dataset, which contains more than 60 years of valuable ecological data.

Your qualities

You are an enterprising researcher with expertise in the ecology of saltmarshes and saline vegetation communities, and a broad interest in the Wadden Sea and coastal ecosystems. You are able to work effectively under time pressure and manage your workload to meet deadlines. You are motivated, proactive, collaborative, client-focused, and possess strong communication skills.

In Addition, You Have

a completed relevant academic degree in the Natural or Life Sciences, with a specialisation in Wadden Sea and coastal ecosystems. A PhD in a field relevant to this position would be an advantage;
knowledge of saltmarsh vegetation;
experience with nature-based solutions;
strong report-writing skills;
experience in applying statistical analyses to long-term and spatial datasets;
a full Category B driving licence;
proficiency in Dutch would be an advantage.

In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about language level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale) C1.

We offer

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include:

working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8,3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. We offer, depending on your experience, a competitive gross salary of between € 3,554.- and € 5,698.- for a full-time working week of 36 hours, in accordance with the CLA Wageningen Research (scale 10). Additionally, for this role a contract for 32 to 36 hours can be discussed. We initially offer a one-year contract, with the possibility of renewal subject to satisfactory performance and depending on the organisation’s financial situation.

We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help.

Coming from abroad

Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees.

Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. If you come with a partner, we offer a Dual Career group program organized by our Welcome Center (https://wcfv.nl/en/home/global/our-services/happy-landing-and-living/). This program helps your partner to get familiar with the Dutch culture, labour market and assists your partner to find a job.

Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/expats-new-international-staff) page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands.

Your job

Post-doc to engage stakeholders in co-producing solutions for climate justice and socially desirable biomass uses

We are looking for a highly motivated post-doctoral researcher. Do you want to work on the big challenges of climate (in)justice in the global North and South, and on the desired use of biomass across Europe? Do you want to work in two large projects with more than ten case studies across the world by engaging with a wide range of stakeholders and co-producing mental models, scenarios, and solutions on these issues? Do you want to work in large interdisciplinary teams? Then maybe this is the job for you!

As post-doctoral researcher you will be involved in two large European projects that recently started – BALANSED and Just in Clime. Both deal with some of the largest (environmental) issues that the world is facing today. The overall topic of Just in Clime relates to climate change impacts, the possible solutions that are put forward, and particularly issues with climate justice that this raises, also between the Global North and the Global South. The overall topic of BALANSED relates to the different ways biomass can be used (for food, feed, biofuel, etc.) and how these uses can be socially desirable. Despite topical differences, both projects have a similar approach to centralising stakeholders and stakeholder perspectives, with a large focus on a process of co-producing solutions to the issues of climate justice and biomass uses. Series of workshops in multiple case studies are planned to engage with stakeholders. In both projects, issues are seen as complex/messy problems that need a systemic approach to understand how systems function and how they are perceived by stakeholders. A range of methods and tools will be used to in a flexible methodology that is catered to specific case-study circumstances, but with similar elements to facilitate synthesis and upscaling. One crucial tool in both projects is a group-model building tool called Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping. This tool will be used to co-produce ‘mental models’ of how stakeholders perceive the system, focusing on feedbacks and complex interactions. An increased understanding of how stakeholders perceive problems and value possible solutions is one of the main outputs of the part of the work. Note that there is no need to be familiar with the specifics of FCMs.

As post-doctoral researcher, you will contribute to activities in both projects – BALANSED and Just in Clime. With a small team of researchers within the Environmental Systems Analysis Group (ESA), you will be responsible for streamlining the process, methods, and co-production of mental models and FCMs and linking outputs to other parts of the projects. Overall, you will closely interact with many other partners in both projects, both scientific and case study partners, and act as a main contact person for ensuring co-produced outcomes fit objectives of local case studies, of social learning and deliberation, and useful outcomes for quantitative models.

Concretely, Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

Develop a (flexible) methodology to co-produce knowledge with stakeholders
Help executing workshops and interviews
Develop mental models that allow understanding of stakeholder perspectives
Summarise, synthesise, and upscale case-study findings to European recommendations
Work with a large variety of scientific partners from both qualitative social sciences and quantitative environmental modellers

Your team

You will work with colleagues within ESA to form a core team to execute activities, but also closely with partners across Europe and the world in the context of both BALANSED and Just in Clime. You will be stationed in Wageningen, but you are expected to travel regularly to case studies to assist with the stakeholder engagement work.

We are the Environmental Systems Analysis Group, where we advance understanding of complex systems, including interconnected challenges across food, biodiversity, water, and climate, requiring integrated, nexus-based approaches linking environmental and societal processes across scales. The sub-group that you will be part of – Empower Sustainable Futures – is specifically working on stakeholder engagement and human-nature relationships.

BALANSED and Just in Clime total about 30 partners across Europe and the world, many of which you will interact with, providing a rich interdisciplinary knowledge base.

This position is unique in that it relates to applying the same methodology and the same tool, but in two very different large projects. First and foremost, we are looking for someone who is comfortable and has experience with working in larger interdisciplinary projects. Given these considerations, we prefer someone with a few years of working experience after PhD graduation.

broad academic skills and you are a dedicated, creative individual with excellent communication and collaboration skills

Duties

In this role, you will evaluate laboratory capabilities, conduct on-site and virtual audits, and serve as the program’s subject matter expert in Organic Chemistry by Liquid Chromatography. Process initial and renewal applications for laboratory accreditation.

Make recommendations to the Laboratory Accreditation Unit supervisor on whether laboratories can produce accurate and defensible analytical data.
Prepare correspondence informing laboratories of their accreditation status and maintain accurate records in the accreditation database.
Serve as the program’s liquid chromatography specialist, reviewing documentation and analytical data generated through LC/MS/MS instrumentation.
Conduct on-site and virtual audits of laboratories, either independently or as the organic chemistry specialist on an audit team.
Prepare clear, detailed audit reports and recommend corrective actions to improve laboratory procedures.
Track and verify laboratory compliance with audit findings.

A minimum of five (5) years of experience employed in the conduct of bench scale laboratory testing, using similar methods and techniques for which auditing services would be provided.

You will work with colleagues on several projects simultaneously, with responsibilities allocated according to capacity and individual interests. Engagement with clients and other stakeholders is an integral part of our work.

Your Responsibilities As a Saltmarsh Ecology Researcher Include

carrying out annual monitoring of sediment accretion and vegetation development across various saltmarshes in the Wadden Sea;
analysing and interpreting monitoring data;
writing reports for clients;
assisting in the acquisition of new projects and the preparation of research proposals;
publishing and presenting your research in scientific journals and at conferences.

Wageningen Marine Research

Your primary area of work will be the Dutch Wadden Sea, although opportunities may also arise to contribute to projects elsewhere in the Netherlands and internationally. Wageningen Marine Research (https://www.wur.nl/en/about-wur/our-research/wageningen-marine-research) (WMR) is a leading organisation in the Netherlands in the field of marine ecological data collection, covering benthic fauna, marine mammals, fish, birds, coral, shellfish, and more. Many of these datasets have been collected and maintained using standardised methodologies for decades. In this role, you will contribute to the continuation and development of the saltmarsh monitoring dataset, which contains more than 60 years of valuable ecological data.

Your qualities

You are an enterprising researcher with expertise in the ecology of saltmarshes and saline vegetation communities, and a broad interest in the Wadden Sea and coastal ecosystems. You are able to work effectively under time pressure and manage your workload to meet deadlines. You are motivated, proactive, collaborative, client-focused, and possess strong communication skills.

In Addition, You Have

a completed relevant academic degree in the Natural or Life Sciences, with a specialisation in Wadden Sea and coastal ecosystems. A PhD in a field relevant to this position would be an advantage;
knowledge of saltmarsh vegetation;
experience with nature-based solutions;
strong report-writing skills;
experience in applying statistical analyses to long-term and spatial datasets;
a full Category B driving licence;
proficiency in Dutch would be an advantage.

Your job

As an Environmental Technology Researcher at Wageningen Livestock Research, you will work on innovative solutions for emission reduction and sustainable manure processing. Please note that an excellent command of Dutch is essential for this role.

You will develop, investigate and support technological applications that contribute to a circular and future-proof livestock sector. Combining applied research with systems analysis, you will work both in the laboratory and on-site at livestock farms and manure processing facilities to test and optimise technologies under practical conditions. You will also use modelling and scenario analysis to assess the potential impact of new technologies at both regional and national levels.

Your Responsibilities As An Environmental Technology Researcher Will Include

designing and carrying out research into manure processing technologies, including anaerobic digestion, drying and nutrient recovery from manure;
measuring ammonia and greenhouse gas emissions from manure storage and processing systems;
analysing and optimising environmental technologies used in livestock farming and advising on future technological developments;
translating research findings into practical applications for the agricultural sector and government;
collaborating with fellow researchers, industry partners, government bodies and other stakeholders;
contributing to innovative projects focused on circular agriculture, renewable energy and sustainable farming.

Your Team

You will join a team of around 40 colleagues - including researchers, project leaders, measurement technicians and laboratory analysts - who are working together to develop innovative solutions for the livestock sector of the future. As a researcher, you will collaborate within the Emissions and Manure Valorisation (https://www.wur.nl/en/research/livestock-research/greenhouse-gases-livestock-farming) multidisciplinary project teams.

Within the department, you will work alongside an enthusiastic group of approximately 40 colleagues with diverse expertise and responsibilities. The team also collaborates extensively with other parts of Wageningen University & Research and with a broad network of external partners.

You will be based within the Emissions and Manure Valorisation department of Livestock Research. (https://www.wur.nl/en/about-wur/our-research/wageningen-livestock-research)

Our Mission

The livestock sector faces significant challenges. Reducing ammonia and greenhouse gas emissions is essential for achieving a sustainable future and maintaining the sector's licence to operate. The Environmental Technology and Manure Valorisation team develops and evaluates technologies that reduce emissions and nutrient losses from manure. At the same time, we increasingly view animal manure as a valuable resource. By converting manure into renewable energy, supporting circular applications and developing new bio-based products, we contribute to a resilient agricultural sector that is less dependent on fossil resources.

You are a proactive and results-oriented researcher who works effectively both independently and as part of multidisciplinary teams. Post-doc to engage stakeholders in co-producing solutions for climate justice and socially desirable biomass uses

We are looking for a highly motivated post-doctoral researcher. Do you want to work in two large projects with more than ten case studies across the world by engaging with a wide range of stakeholders and co-producing mental models, scenarios, and solutions on these issues? Do you want to work in large interdisciplinary teams? Then maybe this is the job for you!

As post-doctoral researcher you will be involved in two large European projects that recently started – BALANSED and Just in Clime. Both deal with some of the largest (environmental) issues that the world is facing today. The overall topic of Just in Clime relates to climate change impacts, the possible solutions that are put forward, and particularly issues with climate justice that this raises, also between the Global North and the Global South. The overall topic of BALANSED relates to the different ways biomass can be used (for food, feed, biofuel, etc.) and how these uses can be socially desirable. Despite topical differences, both projects have a similar approach to centralising stakeholders and stakeholder perspectives, with a large focus on a process of co-producing solutions to the issues of climate justice and biomass uses. Series of workshops in multiple case studies are planned to engage with stakeholders. In both projects, issues are seen as complex/messy problems that need a systemic approach to understand how systems function and how they are perceived by stakeholders. A range of methods and tools will be used to in a flexible methodology that is catered to specific case-study circumstances, but with similar elements to facilitate synthesis and upscaling. One crucial tool in both projects is a group-model building tool called Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping. This tool will be used to co-produce ‘mental models’ of how stakeholders perceive the system, focusing on feedbacks and complex interactions. An increased understanding of how stakeholders perceive problems and value possible solutions is one of the main outputs of the part of the work. Note that there is no need to be familiar with the specifics of FCMs.

As post-doctoral researcher, you will contribute to activities in both projects – BALANSED and Just in Clime. With a small team of researchers within the Environmental Systems Analysis Group (ESA), you will be responsible for streamlining the process, methods, and co-production of mental models and FCMs and linking outputs to other parts of the projects. Overall, you will closely interact with many other partners in both projects, both scientific and case study partners, and act as a main contact person for ensuring co-produced outcomes fit objectives of local case studies, of social learning and deliberation, and useful outcomes for quantitative models.

We are the Environmental Systems Analysis Group, where we advance understanding of complex systems, including interconnected challenges across food, biodiversity, water, and climate, requiring integrated, nexus-based approaches linking environmental and societal processes across scales. BALANSED and Just in Clime total about 30 partners across Europe and the world, many of which you will interact with, providing a rich interdisciplinary knowledge base.

Prepare clear, detailed audit reports and recommend corrective actions to improve laboratory procedures.
Track and verify laboratory compliance with audit findings.
